implementation_notes: Pydantic v2 is the declared mapper: define the boundary shape as a `BaseModel`, convert in one line with `UserDto.model_validate(user, from_attributes=True)` (or `UserDto(**user.model_dump())` when the domain object is itself a model) and go back with `model_dump()`/`model_dump_json()`. Validation, aliasing (`Field(validation_alias=...)`), defaults and coercion are declared on the DTO instead of coded in the mapper, so the translation rules stay reviewable and the domain class keeps no framework import. Choose it when payloads cross a trust boundary or evolve often; prefer hand-written functions when the mapping is small, when the domain must not depend on pydantic, or when the conversion needs real logic rather than field rules.
code_sketch:
class UserDto(BaseModel):                          # the mapper, declared
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
    id: int
    name: str = Field(validation_alias="full_name")   # declared rename
    is_admin: bool = False                            # declared default

dto = UserDto.model_validate(user)                 # invocation at the boundary
user = User(id=dto.id, full_name=dto.name, is_admin=dto.is_admin)
pitfalls: `from_attributes=True` reads attributes loosely: a renamed domain attribute quietly falls back to the declared default instead of failing, so the mapping still needs tests.
Defaults swallow absent fields - distinguish absent from false with `model_fields_set` (or make the field required) when the difference matters.
Extra keys are ignored by default; `extra='forbid'` is what turns an unexpected payload into an error instead of a silent drop.

variants.name: Hand-written mapping functions over dataclasses
variants.idiom_name: from_dict / to_dict functions plus @dataclass domain and DTO types
variants.implementation_notes: The stdlib route needs no dependency: `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` value objects plus a `mappings.py` module with `user_from_dict(d)` and `user_to_dict(u)`, using `dataclasses.asdict` only for the trivially symmetric part and explicit field reads where the names or units differ. Choose it when the domain must not import a validation framework, when the mapping has real logic (units, nested identity, defaults), or when the project deliberately keeps dependencies thin; pydantic earns its place when the same shape must be validated at an untrusted edge. Frozen dataclasses additionally make the mapped value immutable, so an accidental shared reference cannot mutate the translation's output.
pitfalls: `dataclasses.asdict` is recursive and deep-copies through containers, so a custom nested object leaks into the DTO unless the mapper converts it explicitly.
Dict access policy is invisible: `d["id"]` fails loudly but `d.get(...)` with a default silently accepts a missing field - choose per field and stay consistent.
`slots=True` blocks ad-hoc attributes that mappers sometimes set as scratch space; the mapping must build the target through its constructor.
